mainTopic: The label שומרת יבם in a סוטה ברייתא, and whether a יבמה after מאמר (or after מאמר and a גט) may eat תרומה.
overview: The amud opens by asking how a ברייתא about סוטה can call a woman a שומרת יבם after her יבם was intimate with her, since רב holds that such relations acquire her fully. The גמרא first answers 'like שמואל', but rejects that answer, since the whole discussion only matters according to רב. It then explains the ברייתא as a case where the יבם first did מאמר, following בית שמאי. It defends the ברייתא's wording by comparing the pair ארוסה and שומרת יבם to the pair נשואה and כנוסה. רב פפא and רב נחמן בר יצחק then give other ways to explain the ברייתא: one by pointing to a particular תנא, and one by extending the oath (גלגול). Next, a new topic begins: whether a יבמה after מאמר may eat תרומה. רב חנינא's report of רבי יוחנן fits no תנא, so רבין gives a corrected version. In that version, everyone agrees on plain מאמר and on a brother who is a חלל, and רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue only when a גט was given, each with his reasoning. Finally, the גמרא returns to the משנה and begins a question to שמואל about a כהן גדול who betrothed a minor who grew up while betrothed to him.

steps.title: How can she still be called a woman waiting for her יבם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's wording. Once the יבם has been intimate with her, רב says he acquired her fully, so she is his wife and no longer a שומרת יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: You call her a שומרת יבם? She is his full wife, because רב said that relations acquire her for everything!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the label 'שומרת יבם' in the ברייתא. After relations she should count as a fully married wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, relations with a יבמה acquire her completely, even if the יבם did not intend יבום. So a woman who has had relations with her יבם is simply his wife. Calling her a 'woman waiting for her יבם' seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: a widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום or חליצה
his full, proper wife
he acquired her for all matters

phrases.english: Do you call her a woman waiting for her yavam?
phrases.notes: This is about the ברייתא quoted just before, which speaks of a שומרת יבם whom the יבם was intimate with.

phrases.english: She is his proper wife,
for Rav said: He has acquired her for everything!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא brought in the preceding discussion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's description of the woman as a שומרת יבם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב, relations with a יבמה make her a full wife. A woman with full wife status cannot still be called a שומרת יבם.

steps.title: Answer: the ברייתא follows שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא can follow שמואל, who holds that relations acquire a יבמה only for the laws written in the section of יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows שמואל, who said that he acquired her only for the matters stated in the section of יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא can follow שמואל instead of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, relations with a יבמה acquire her only for the rules of יבום itself. For other areas of law, like סוטה, she is not yet considered his full wife. So the label 'שומרת יבם' still works for שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: the matters written in the Torah's section about יבום

phrases.english: It is like Shmuel, who said:
He acquired her only
for the matters stated in the section.
phrases.notes: He means the Torah's section about יבום in דברים 25.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 1 by attributing the ברייתא to שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a different אמורא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא must fit רב's view that relations acquire fully.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא fits שמואל, for whom she is not yet a full wife regarding סוטה.

steps.title: Challenged: the whole proof only matters for רב
steps.stepSummary: The answer from שמואל does not help. The proof was brought only for רב's opinion, and רב holds that relations acquire her fully.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole reason for this discussion is only according to רב. But רב said he acquired her for everything!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the previous answer. The question is raised for רב, so explaining the ברייתא like שמואל does not help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion about a כהן's חופה with a woman forbidden to him only matters for רב, who gives that חופה legal weight. So the ברייתא must be explained within רב's view. Under רב's view, the problem from step 1 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: the whole reason is only...

phrases.english: The whole reason is only according to Rav.
phrases.notes: The question of whether a כהן's חופה with a forbidden woman counts was only raised according to רב.

phrases.english: But Rav said: He acquired her for everything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2 and brings back the challenge of step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the ברייתא follows שמואל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The whole discussion is framed according to רב, so the answer has to work for רב.

steps.title: The case is where he did מאמר, following בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks about a case where the יבם first did מאמר with her. It follows בית שמאי, who say מאמר acquires her completely, so the later relations do not make her his full wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are dealing with a case where he did מאמר with her. This follows בית שמאי, who say that מאמר is a complete acquisition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that works even for רב. The ברייתא is about a יבמה with whom the יבם first did מאמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, מאמר fully acquires the יבמה and removes the יבום bond. After that, the relations are not acts of יבום, so they do not make her his full wife. That is why she can still be described the way the ברייתא does.

keyTerms.meaning: with what case are we dealing here?
a rabbinic form of betrothal of a יבמה, using money or a document
the school of שמאי
a complete acquisition

steps.confusionAlert: This only works for בית שמאי. For בית הלל, מאמר does not fully acquire her.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
For example, where he did levirate betrothal with her,
phrases.notes: After the מאמר, he was intimate with her, but not for the sake of יבום.

phrases.english: and it is Beit Shammai, who say:
Levirate betrothal acquires completely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge brought back in step 3, this time within רב's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) plus attributing it to בית שמאי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The relations in the ברייתא would be יבום and would make her a full wife.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מאמר already acquired her, so the relations are not יבום and do not make her a full wife.

steps.title: Then she is the same as a betrothed woman
steps.stepSummary: If the יבמה was acquired by מאמר, she is just like an ארוסה. Why would the ברייתא list both?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this is the same as a betrothed woman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. A יבמה with מאמר seems no different from an ארוסה, so listing both looks repetitive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the ארוסה and the שומרת יבם as two separate cases. If the שומרת יבם is really betrothed through מאמר, the two cases seem identical, and the second mention adds nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
that is the same as
a betrothed woman (after קידושין, before נשואין)

phrases.english: If so, that is the same as a betrothed woman?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case set up in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the שומרת יבם was acquired through מאמר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, the ברייתא's two listed cases, ארוסה and שומרת יבם, are the same case.

steps.title: His own wife versus his brother's wife
steps.stepSummary: The pair נשואה and כנוסה also look the same, yet they are explained as his own wife versus his brother's. In the same way, ארוסה means his own betrothed and שומרת יבם means his brother's widow betrothed to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: By your logic, aren't 'married' and 'taken in' the same thing? Rather, 'married' is his own wife and 'taken in' is his brother's. Here too, 'betrothed' is his own and 'שומרת יבם' is his brother's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to another pair in the list that also looks repetitive and showing how that pair is explained. It then applies the same explanation to ארוסה and שומרת יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list already contains a near-duplicate, נשואה and כנוסה, which must mean his own wife versus his brother's widow whom he married through יבום. Following the same pattern, ארוסה is his own betrothed woman and שומרת יבם is his brother's widow betrothed to him by מאמר. The cases are similar but come from different sources.

keyTerms.meaning: and according to your reasoning
a married woman
a woman 'taken in' as a wife
his own / his fellow's

steps.whatToRemember: Each similar-sounding pair in the list is explained as his own woman versus his brother's widow.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: נְשׂוּאָה וּכְנוּסָה לָאו חֲדָא מִילְּתָא הִיא?!
phrases.english: aren't a married woman and a fully married woman one matter?!
Rather: married means his own wife,
and fully married means his fellow's.
phrases.notes: 'His fellow's' here means his brother's widow, whom he married through יבום.

phrases.english: Here too: betrothed means his own,
and the woman waiting for her yavam is his fellow's.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְטַעְמָיךְ, נְשׂוּאָה וּכְנוּסָה לָאו חֲדָא מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by comparing the case to another pair in the same list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-question (ולטעמיך) followed by a parallel explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ארוסה and שומרת יבם (with מאמר) are the same case listed twice.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are parallel but different: his own betrothed versus his brother's widow betrothed to him.

steps.title: רב פפא: the ברייתא follows a particular תנא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers differently. The ברייתא follows a תנא who says a man may warn his betrothed woman so that she drinks once she is married. This approach does not depend on the question about a כהן's חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it follows this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: one may not warn a betrothed woman to make her drink while she is betrothed, but one may warn her to make her drink once she is married.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a completely different way to explain the ברייתא, by linking it to a specific תנא's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא answers רבא's difficulty in a way unrelated to the question about the כהן's חופה: he says the ברייתא simply follows a תנא who allows a warning given during ארוסין to lead to drinking after נשואין. On this approach, the earlier proof falls away and the questions about מאמר are not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: a sage of the משנה period
warning a wife (קינוי) not to be alone with a certain man
to make her drink the סוטה waters

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא explains the ברייתא through a תנא's view about warning an ארוסה, not through the question about a כהן's חופה.

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: הַאי תַּנָּא הוּא,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is this tanna,
as it is taught in a baraita:
One may not warn a betrothed woman
in order to make her drink while she is betrothed,
but one may warn her
in order to make her drink when she is married.
phrases.notes: Even if she was alone with the man while still betrothed, she drinks after the marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: הַאי תַּנָּא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a separate approach to the ברייתא, not built on steps 2 through 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows something about the legal effect of a כהן's חופה with a forbidden woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא simply follows the תנא who allows a warning given during ארוסין to lead to drinking after נשואין.

steps.title: The oath can be extended to cover the betrothal time
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a third answer: the ברייתא works through גלגול, extending the oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: it works by extending the oath.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers another answer to the question from the earlier steps. He says the woman's oath can be stretched to include her betrothal period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She does not drink the waters because of what happened while she was only betrothed. But once she must swear about her time as a married woman, the oath can be extended to cover the betrothal time too. This avoids the whole question of the earlier answers.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'rolling'. Extending an oath that is already required so it also covers other matters.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
By means of extension.
phrases.notes: He means that once she has to swear about her married time, her betrothal time can be added onto the same oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: עַל יְדֵי גִלְגּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer, given alongside רב פפא's in step 7: instead of linking the ברייתא to a specific תנא, it explains the betrothal period through extending the oath (גלגול).
steps.terutzResolutionType: New mechanism: the oath is extended (גלגול).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא needed a special case about a betrothed woman drinking later.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her oath about her married period can be extended to include the betrothal period.

steps.title: מאמר with a יבמה disqualifies her from תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא reports in the name of רבי יוחנן: if a יבם does מאמר with his יבמה and he has a brother, she can no longer eat תרומה, even if both are from כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא sent in the name of רבי יוחנן: If a man does מאמר with his יבמה and he has a brother, then even if he is a כהן and she is a כהן's daughter, he has made her unable to eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי יוחנן rules that doing מאמר with a יבמה, when there is another brother, stops her from eating תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law the other brother can still do יבום with her, but after the מאמר the רבנן do not allow him to. So she is waiting for a relationship that is forbidden by the רבנן. That is why she loses her right to eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic kind of betrothal that a יבם does with his יבמה before יבום.
His יבמה: his dead brother's widow, who is waiting for יבום.
The holy portion of produce that only כהנים and their households may eat.
A woman who is a כהן's daughter.

steps.whyThisMatters: This statement sets up the whole discussion that follows about whether a woman waiting for a forbidden relationship may eat תרומה.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח רַב חֲנִינָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥanina sent in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
One who performs levirate betrothal with his yevama
[and he has a brother],
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have these words. The square brackets show they belong in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: even if he is a priest and she is the daughter of a priest,
he has disqualified her from teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח רַב חֲנִינָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the סוטה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מאמר with a יבמה, when there is another brother, disqualifies her from תרומה.

steps.title: Which תנא could hold this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's statement fits neither רבי מאיר nor רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? If you say רבי מאיר: he said a woman waiting for a forbidden relationship cannot eat only when it is forbidden by Torah law. Did he say so when it is forbidden only by the רבנן? And if you say רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון: they say she eats even when the relationship is forbidden by Torah law. Then it is obvious that she eats when it is forbidden only by the רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא could agree with רבי יוחנן. It tries both sides of the known argument, and neither one works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר takes away תרומה only when the forbidden relationship is forbidden by Torah law, but here it is forbidden only by the רבנן. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון let her eat even in a Torah-forbidden case, so they would surely let her eat here. So the statement as רב חנינא reported it fits nobody.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is waiting for a relationship that is forbidden to her.
Forbidden by Torah law.
Forbidden only by the רבנן.
'Does it need to be said?' Used when something should be obvious.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is the strict side and רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון are the lenient side. Each one fails for the opposite reason: for רבי מאיר the case is too light to matter, and for רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון the ruling would be too strict.

phrases.english: According to whom?
If we say it is according to Rabbi Meir,
say that Rabbi Meir said
a woman reserved for an invalid act of intercourse
may not eat, when it is forbidden by Torah law;
but when it is forbidden by rabbinic law, did he say so?
Rather, it is according to Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon.
Now, if a woman reserved for intercourse forbidden by Torah law
may eat,
is it necessary to say so when it is forbidden by rabbinic law?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חנינא's report of רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that מאמר disqualifies her from תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Neither side of the תנאים argument supports disqualifying her because of a relationship that is forbidden only by the רבנן.

steps.title: רבין's corrected version: the cases everyone agrees on
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports רבי יוחנן differently. After plain מאמר everyone agrees she eats, and if there is a brother who is a חלל everyone agrees she does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רבין came, he said: If he did מאמר with his יבמה, all agree she eats. If he has a brother who is a חלל, all agree she does not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב חנינא's version didn't work, the גמרא brings רבין's version of רבי יוחנן's teaching. It starts with two cases that everyone agrees on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain מאמר does not take away her תרומה, which removes the difficulty from step 10. A brother who is a חלל is different: by Torah law a relationship with him would disqualify her (a ביאה פסולה), so she counts as waiting for a disqualifying relationship, and all agree she cannot eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees.
A כהן's son who lost the status of כהונה, for example the son of a divorced woman and a כהן.

phrases.english: Rather, when Ravin came, he said:
If he performed levirate betrothal with his yevama,
all agree that she may eat.
If he has a brother who is a ḥalal,
all agree that she may not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב חנינא's version, which failed in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrected report of the original statement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן said that מאמר alone disqualifies her from תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Plain מאמר does not disqualify her. Only a brother who is a חלל does, and everyone agrees on both cases.

steps.title: The argument when he gave her a גט
steps.stepSummary: The only argument is when the יבם gave her a גט after the מאמר. רבי יוחנן says she eats, and ריש לקיש says she does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argued only when he gave her a גט. רבי יוחנן said: she eats. ריש לקיש said: she does not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין finishes his report by naming the one case that is argued about. That case is when the יבם gives her a גט after the מאמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא states the two opinions without giving the reasons. רבי יוחנן is lenient and lets her eat תרומה, while ריש לקיש is strict and does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A bill of divorce. Here it is given to undo the מאמר.
'They argued only about…' This limits the argument to one case.
רבי שמעון בן לקיש, רבי יוחנן's frequent partner in argument.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבין: after plain מאמר she eats תרומה, and with a brother who is a חלל she does not. Only when a גט was given after the מאמר do רבי יוחנן (she eats) and ריש לקיש (she does not) argue.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁנָּתַן לָהּ גֵּט.
phrases.english: They disagreed only where he gave her a bill of divorce.
phrases.notes: He means a גט given after the מאמר, to undo it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: She may eat.
Reish Lakish said: She may not eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁנָּתַן לָהּ גֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבין's report by stating the one case that is argued about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a גט was given after the מאמר, רבי יוחנן says she eats תרומה and ריש לקיש says she does not.

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן says she may eat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that even רבי מאיר forbids תרומה only when she is waiting for a relationship that is forbidden by Torah law. Here the problem is only מדרבנן, so she eats.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said she may eat. Even according to רבי מאיר, who says she may not eat, that is only when she is waiting for a relationship forbidden by Torah law. If it is forbidden only by the רבנן, she eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's position from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר says a woman who is waiting for a forbidden relationship with a כהן cannot eat תרומה. רבי יוחנן limits this to a relationship that is forbidden by Torah law. After מאמר and a גט, the bond of יבום still exists by Torah law. Only the רבנן forbid them to finish the יבום, so רבי מאיר's rule does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: She eats (תרומה)
She is waiting / set aside for
A forbidden relationship (one that would disqualify her)
By Torah law
By rabbinic law

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: she eats —

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר אֵינָהּ אוֹכֶלֶת,
phrases.english: even according to Rabbi Meir, who said she does not eat,
that applies only when she is waiting
for a relationship forbidden by Torah law,
but if it is forbidden by the Rabbis, she eats.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר אוֹכֶלֶת אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר's restriction applies only to a Torah-level forbidden relationship, and a rabbinic one does not stop her from eating תרומה.

steps.title: Why ריש לקיש says she may not eat
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that even רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון allow her to eat only in a case of קידושין, since קידושין can make a woman eat תרומה. A גט never makes a woman eat, so here she does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said she does not eat. Even רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, who say she eats, mean only a case like קידושין, which can make a woman eat in other cases. Here, since a גט cannot make a woman eat in any other case, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind ריש לקיש's position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון let a betrothed woman eat even though she is unfit for the כהן. ריש לקיש says that leniency works only because the act involved, קידושין, normally does make a woman eat תרומה. Here the last act was a גט, and a גט normally takes a woman's right to eat away, so the leniency does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: It (the act) can give her the right to eat
In another case
Here (in our case of a גט)

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said: she does not eat —
even according to Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon
who say she eats,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ לְהַאֲכִיל בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
phrases.english: that applies only where it can make her eat in another case,
phrases.notes: "It" is the act of קידושין, which can make a woman fit for a כהן eat תרומה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּאֵין לוֹ לְהַאֲכִיל
phrases.english: but here, since it cannot make her eat
in any other case — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר אֵינָהּ אוֹכֶלֶת אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for ריש לקיש's opposing ruling in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון works only with an act that can make a woman eat תרומה, and a גט never does.

steps.title: Can't a גט also make a woman eat?
steps.stepSummary: A possible challenge to ריש לקיש: a גט can make a woman eat, since a divorced כהן's daughter goes back and eats in her father's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: here too it can make her eat, as in the case of a woman who returns to her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible challenge to ריש לקיש's claim that a גט never makes a woman eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a כהן's daughter who married a non-כהן. When he divorces her, she goes back to her father's house and may eat תרומה again. So it seems a גט can make a woman eat, and ריש לקיש's distinction is in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible objection)
A woman who returns (to her father's house)

phrases.english: And if you will say:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי יֵשׁ לוֹ לְהַאֲכִילָהּ בְּחוֹזֶרֶת —
phrases.english: here too it can make her eat, in the case of one who returns —
phrases.notes: He means a כהן's daughter whose non-כהן husband divorced her. She goes back to eating תרומה in her father's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי יֵשׁ לוֹ לְהַאֲכִילָהּ בְּחוֹזֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given for ריש לקיש in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that a גט never makes a woman eat תרומה in any case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A divorced כהן's daughter returns to eat in her father's house, so a גט does seem to make a woman eat.

steps.title: The returning daughter is fully cut off
steps.stepSummary: The returning daughter is fully cut off from her husband and close to her father's house. This יבמה is still bound to the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who returns is cut off from him and is close to her father's house. But this one is still bound to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and defends ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the returning-daughter case, the גט itself does not make her eat. It cuts her off completely, and she simply goes back to her father's household. Our יבמה, even after the גט, is still tied to the יבם until חליצה, so nothing brings back her right to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: She is cut off from him
Her (father's) household
She is bound to him

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: a rabbinic-level forbidden relationship does not stop her from eating, so she eats. ריש לקיש: a גט, unlike קידושין, never makes a woman eat, and she is still bound to the יבם, so she does not eat.

phrases.english: one who returns is cut off from him,
and is close to the household,
phrases.notes: "The household" here means her father's house, where she eats as a כהן's daughter.

phrases.english: but this one is bound to him.
phrases.notes: The יבמה is still tied to the יבם until he does חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹזֶרֶת פָּסְקָה מִינֵּיהּ וּקְרוֹבָה לְבֵי נָשָׁא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a divorced daughter goes back to eating תרומה, a גט can make a woman eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The returning daughter is fully cut off and goes back to her father's house. The יבמה remains bound to the יבם, so the גט gives her nothing.

steps.title: A כהן גדול betroths a minor who grows up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's case of widowed or divorced women. רבי חייא בר יוסף begins asking שמואל about a כהן גדול who betrothed a קטנה who became a בוגרת while betrothed to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: "They were widowed or divorced, etc." רבי חייא בר יוסף asked שמואל: a כהן גדול who betrothed a minor, and she became an adult while with him...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting the משנה and sets up a question. The full question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught rules for women who become unfit for a כהן. Here the woman was fit when she was betrothed, but she became a בוגרת while still betrothed, and a כהן גדול may not marry a בוגרת. This sets up a question about her status, which the גמרא finishes next.

keyTerms.meaning: They were widowed or divorced (quote from the משנה)
He asked of him
High Priest
A minor girl
She became an adult (a בוגרת)

phrases.english: They were widowed or divorced, etc.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Yosef asked Shmuel:
A High Priest who betrothed a minor
and she matured while under him,
phrases.notes: "Under him" means while she was still betrothed to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by going back to the משנה's clause about widowed or divorced women.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The status of a woman whom a כהן גדול betrothed as a קטנה, if she became a בוגרת while betrothed to him. The full question continues on the next amud.
